headline: Opposition to data centers has spread so fast across the US that politicians of both parties now feel forced to take a position before the midterm elections.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a detailed BBC look at a spreading political issue, though based partly on early polling.
importance_line: Residents near planned sites, voters and candidates in both parties are affected, and the claim that data centers could decide elections rests on early polling in which they rank behind the Iran war and the economy.
summary: The BBC reports that groups opposing data centers more than doubled to 833 in the first months of this year, according to Data Center Watch, and that politicians including Arizona's Democratic governor Katie Hobbs and Texas's Republican governor Greg Abbott have shifted position, putting some Republicans at odds with President Donald Trump, who called the backlash a "sick conspiracy". It adds that Brookings found a new data center creates 100 to 200 local jobs, fewer than industry claims, and that most moratoriums last one to three years, so the political mood could change.
notes: Own reporting by the BBC; the senator's adviser is anonymous.
